summary: Steel lookout tower on Highway 72 in Reynolds County, Mark Twain National Forest; 1934 construction under way, built by CCC Company 732; NHLR-registered August 2026.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a glassed-in lookout room and finial; register lists it as model MC-39

access.note: Forest Service land with free parking in the tower area (Salem News). No source read confirms whether the tower can be climbed; a hike write-up mentions a locked gate further west on Highway 72.

visit.trail_note: A Salem News hike feature gives directions from Highway 72 in Reynolds County, turning into the tower parking area. A Trail of Tears sign stands across the highway from the tower.

events.note: Foundation being dug by November 22, 1934; newspaper said completion would follow about a week after the pour. Completion date not confirmed in sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 newspaper gives 99 feet, nine inches to the floor of the cab, as a plan. The 1939 survey description gives about 110 feet high without saying where that height is measured. The two figures may measure different points, so the sources do not establish one agreed height.

notes_for_editor: Built date is not established. The record has none. The only dated construction fact is the November 22, 1934 newspaper item that the foundation was being dug; the 1936 completion date appears in a web search summary citing the Living New Deal database, but livingnewdeal.org returned 403 to our reader, so it is not used and needs a manual check. Height: record height_m 33.5 equals the 1939 survey's 'about 110 feet'. The 1934 cab-floor figure (99 ft 9 in, about 30.4 m) is a plan, not a measured height. The editor should decide which measure the record should carry. Status 'standing' rests on the Salem News description in the present tense and the NPS page, which invites visits; no source read states the tower's condition in 2025 or 2026. Access level 'public' refers to Forest Service land with free parking; climbing is not confirmed. The NHLR entry says 'Nominated by Admin'. The NHLR photo set was not added to the record. Staffing is not stated in any source read; the Salem News credits CCC Company 732, not a lookout crew, with construction.
